name: Twodle
brief: Final project for my C#/.NET class. A partner project where we had to develop a desktop application of our choice. There were nine requirements that we had to pick 8 of to employ, ranging from arrays to threading.
description: Me and my partner built a Twodle game, which is essentially two games of Wordle being played at the same time where each guess applies to both games.  The work was split pretty evenly, with the two of us collaborating on how to do it, and switching off tasks.

name: TV Rex
brief: Developed for TigerHacks 2023, Mizzou's annual hackathon.  The theme for the year was 'media' and it was up to us what we made beyond that.
description: My group made a website that recommends tv shows based on 'list-icles' online.  I worked with the TMDB API to get the information that we were going to use in our website.  It was my first time working with APIs and I spent a lot of time trying to fix issues that came up with the first API we were trying to use, before eventually switching to TMDB.

name: Database Booktracking
brief: Final project for my Databases class.  We had to create our own database and schema and create three functions to interact with the database.
description: I made a basic book tracking program, inspired by Goodreads, but ideally with more customizable reading challenges.  This was my first time using SQL and incorporating it with another program, so I tried to keep it relatively simple for the purpose of this assignment.

name: Portfolio Website
description: This project is the website you're currently looking at.  It is my first time working with html/css since I was in 7th grade and learned basic HTML in my computers class, which also means I retaught myself all of that and much more in order to build this website.

name: Chatroom Client/Server
brief: This project was developed for my Computer Networks course.  We had to develop both the client side and server side of a chatroom application to practice implementing networking requests.
description: It's a relatively bare-bones application (our output had to match the expected output exactly).  This was my first time working with socket programming.  I also worked on an extra credit application that used threading to support multiple clients, but I wasn't able to get it working before the assignment was due (I was running into issues with implementing threading on the client side, and this was my first time using threading and it hadn't been covered in class).

name: Class Labs
brief: The projects on this page are a small snapshot of what I have done in CS, and I have experience with a variety of other topics that I have learned about in my classes and then used in coding lab assignments for those classes.  It feels redundant to create a project listing for each of those (non-project based) labs/class assignments, so instead I am going to cover some of those skills here.
description: These classes include the multipe Data Structures and Algorithms classes, Assembly, etc.  Some of the lab topics include things like linked lists, hash tables, binary trees, graphs, various searching and sorting methods, etc.  These assignments were almost always written in C.

name: Garden Drip
brief: Final project for my Game Development class.  It was a partner project, but rather open-ended.  We had to design a game that showed a strong understanding of Unity game development, relate to the theme Connections in some way, and fall into one of the four project options: core mechanic game, physics based game, procedural generation game, or scientific/engineering visualization game.
description: My teammate and I chose to build a version of a pipe connecting game, where you have to click on the pipes to rotate them to connect the input and output pipes.  Our game used procedural generation to create a unique level each time, using a simplified version of Kruskal's Algorithm, using Union Find to connect the start and end point of the grid.  Then Breadth-First Search was used to prune the maze and find a solution

name: School Bus Stop Sign Detection
brief: Final project for my Digital Image Processing.  We were expected to implement a common image processing pipeline (object detection, feature matching, etc) by either applying it to a new problem or using a new method to implement it.  We were not expected to write all steps ourselves and encourage to use source code or existing algorithms to base our methods on.
description: For this project, I was aware of existing issues where Tesla Self Driving does not stop for school buses.  I knew there was plenty of research done on stop sign detection, so there's no reason that school bus stop sign detection wouldn't be managable.  I decided this project direction in late October 2025.  Two days before I presented it, Waymo recalled their software for the exact same research.  My project relied on training a model to detect school bus stop signs, and then detecting whether at least one light on the stop sign was illuminated.  The model succeeded in detecting the stop sign, but sadly I was unable to get the light detection to work properly (full report on Github).
